newsitem.title: USA: Lawmaker proposes bill to raise Fed accountability.
newsitem.headline: Lawmaker proposes bill to raise Fed accountability.

text.p: Rep. Henry Gonzalez, the ranking Democrat on the House Banking Committee, on Thursday introduced a bill aimed at making the Federal Reserve more accountable to Congress.

The Texas congressman's legislation would, among other things, require the central bank to disclos promptly its monetary policy decisions and would widen the ability of Congress' investigative arm, the General Accounting Office, to scrutinize the Fed's activities.
The provision requiring prompt disclosure of policy decisions would codify a practice the Fed began three years ago.

The legislation would also require that the presidents of the regional Fed banks be appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate, rather than being named by private interests as is now the case.
In a news release announcing the bill, Gonzalez, as he has done in the past, criticized the Fed's management and budgeting practices and cited a need to "clean house" at the agency.
